record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Topological Algebra
record.context_brief: Additive structure of compact subsets of R
record.original_question: Let A be a compact subset of the real line R such that the difference set A − A = {a − a′ : a, a′ ∈ A} is a neighborhood of 0 in R. Must the fourfold sumset A + A + A + A have non-empty interior in R?

evidence.quote: Problem 12 (Banakh). Let A be a compact subset of the real line R such that A − A = {a−a′ : a, a′ ∈ A} is a neighborhood of zero in R. Has the sum A+A+A+A non-empty interior in R?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a compact subset of the real line such that the difference set
$$A - A = \{a - a' : a, a' \in A\}$$
is a neighborhood of $0$ in $\mathbb{R}$ (i.e., contains an open interval around $0$). Must the fourfold sumset
$$A + A + A + A = \{a_1 + a_2 + a_3 + a_4 : a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4 \in A\}$$
have non-empty interior in $\mathbb{R}$?
artifact.category_tag: Additive structure of compact sets in R
artifact.status_search_result: A 2022 paper by T. Banakh, I. Banakh, and E. Jabłońska on products of K-analytic sets in locally compact groups establishes results in the same circle of ideas (e.g., a K-analytic subset $A$ of a locally compact group with $AAAA$ having empty interior must be coverable by countably many closed Haar-null sets), but no source located definitively confirms a positive or negative resolution of the precise question about a compact $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ with $A-A$ a neighborhood of $0$ and the interior of $A+A+A+A$. The status appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Products of K-Analytic Sets in Locally Compact Groups and Kuczma–Ger Classes
status_evidence.snippet: A K-analytic subset A of X can be covered by countably many closed Haar-null sets if the set AAAA has an empty interior in X.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial result by Banakh and collaborators on when fourfold products/sums fail to have interior, but it does not directly settle the compact case in R under the hypothesis that A-A is a neighborhood of 0.

status_evidence.title: Compact sets with large projections and nowhere dense sumset (arXiv:2006.15206)
status_evidence.snippet: For d≥2 there exists a compact set K ⊆ R^d such that the projection of K onto each hyperplane has non-empty interior, but K+K is nowhere dense.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves a related (different) question of Banakh, Jabłońska and Jabłoński; not the one-dimensional A-A/A+A+A+A problem.
